sections.title: Market Pulse: Strong Weekly Gains on Soft Jobs Report and AI Enthusiasm

items.headline: U.S. Markets Close Week Strong, Driven by Weak Jobs Data and Tech Rally
items.summary: U.S. equity markets concluded the week ending August 8, 2026, with significant advances, as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average reached new all-time highs. The rally was primarily fueled by a weaker-than-expected July jobs report, which eased concerns about aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes, coupled with renewed investor enthusiasm for AI-related stocks and generally positive corporate earnings reports. Technology stocks led the charge, while the Energy sector lagged amidst falling oil prices.

items.headline: Airbnb Surges on Strong Outlook
items.summary: Shares of Airbnb ($ABNB) jumped 17% after the company raised its revenue outlook, indicating strong anticipated performance.

items.headline: Nvidia Leads Weekly Tech Gains
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) climbed 11.6% over the past week, significantly contributing to the S&P 500's gains amidst renewed enthusiasm for AI-related stocks.

items.headline: Palantir Experiences Significant Weekly Rally
items.summary: Palantir Technologies Inc. ($PLTR) saw a substantial increase of 39.78% for the week, signaling strong investor confidence.

items.headline: Trade Desk Plunges on Weak Forecast
items.summary: The Trade Desk ($TTD) shares plunged 22% after the company issued a weak forecast, prompting analyst downgrades.

items.headline: AMD Falls Despite Strong Earnings
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices ($AMD) fell 7% for the week, despite beating earnings estimates, due to concerns surrounding its capital expenditures.

items.headline: Solowin Holdings Leads Financial Decliners
items.summary: Solowin Holdings ($AXG) topped the list of decliners in the financials sector for the week, reaching oversold territory based on its 14-day Relative Strength Index.

items.headline: Technology Leads as Energy Lags in Weekly Sector Performance
items.summary: For the week ending August 8, 2026, the Technology sector led all major sectors with a gain of 7.2%, driven by strong performance in AI and semiconductor companies like Nvidia, Broadcom, Intel, and Microsoft. Materials (+4.8%) and Industrials (+3.0%) also saw significant gains. Conversely, the Energy sector was the weakest, declining 3.66% as oil prices eased amid hopes of a de-escalation in Middle East tensions and a potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Investors broadly rotated into growth, high-beta, and large-cap tech stocks, while divesting from energy, commodities, and real estate.

items.headline: Weak July Jobs Report Cools Fed Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a surprising contraction of 23,000 jobs in July, significantly below consensus estimates and marking the weakest employment reading since February. Despite this, the unemployment rate slightly decreased to 4.1%. This unexpectedly soft jobs data led market participants to lower their expectations for a September Federal Reserve rate hike, with futures markets now pricing a roughly 43-44% chance of a 25 basis point increase, down from 55% prior to the report. Additionally, the ISM Services PMI for July registered 54.1, showing strengthening new orders but a contraction in employment, while the prices index increased to 70.3.

items.headline: Key Earnings: Berkshire Hathaway Reports Strong Q2; Airbnb and Trade Desk Diverge
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. ($BRK.A, $BRK.B) released its second-quarter 2026 earnings on August 8, reporting net earnings attributable to shareholders of $25.667 billion, a significant increase from $12.370 billion in Q2 2025. Other notable earnings moves included Airbnb ($ABNB) jumping 17% after raising its revenue outlook, while The Trade Desk ($TTD) plunged 22% following a disappointing forecast. In the financials sector, Hagerty ($HGTY) and Oportun Financial ($OPRT) both beat Q2 earnings estimates and provided solid guidance.
